To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the positive effect of one litter type on the decomposition rate of another litter type can be accounted for by the transfer from the first litter to the second of a resource limiting microbial enzyme activity.

the positive effect of one litter type on the decomposition of another litter type can result from the transfer of a limiting resource to the decomposing litter from a source other than the decomposing litter.

the positive, non-addive effect of clover on oat straw decomposition was due to the transfer to oat straw of a limiting resource other than labile nitrogen, that the soil was the source of that limiting resource, and that this mechanism may explain the positive, nonadditive decomposition observed by other investigators in previous studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how resources are transferred between plants and microbes and between plants and soil.
the mechanisms that explain the positive effect of a leguminous plant on the decomposition of an herbaceous plant.
the role of resource transfer from litter to soil in the non-additive decomposition of mixed litter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the positive, non-addive effect of clover on oat straw decomposition is attributable to the transfer of a limiting mineral nutrient other than N from clover to the oat straw.
the majority of the effect of clover on oat straw decomposition is attributable to the supply of mineral nutrients other than nitrogen from the clover litter to the soil.
clover litter increases decomposition of oat straw by supplying mineral nutrients other than nitrogen, and possibly other limiting resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
positive non-additive decomposition is not necessarily a result of the transfer of resources limiting microbial activity from one litter type to another.
the positive, non-addive effect of clover on oat straw decomposition was due to the transfer from the clover to the oat straw of a limiting resource other than labile N.
the positive effect of one litter species on decomposition of another species can be due to resource transfer, but the identity of the transferred resource is not necessarily N.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of one litter type in a mixed litter system can increase the activity of enzymes involved in decomposition by supplying limiting resources to decomposers that are present on the other litter type.

the presence of clovers and legumes in a forest or grassland may increase the decomposition rate of other species in the same community by providing resources that limit decomposer activity in the other species.
resource transfer can account for non-additivity in decomposition, even if the transferred resource is not N.
